article.headline: GitLab Eases AI Fears As Revenue Climbs 21.3% And Shares Near High
article.deck: GitLab holds 2.1% above its 55.65 buy point, in a buy range that runs to 58.43.
body: GitLab sells one application for the whole software-building process: planning, code, security scans, compliance checks and deployment, sold to teams that would otherwise stitch those tools together. Its newer pitch is the GitLab Duo Agent Platform, which puts AI agents to work alongside developers on planning, coding and security tasks. The company sells in the United States, Europe and Asia Pacific.

The case for the stock is the top line. Revenue rose 21.3% in the July quarter to $286.3 million, and it has grown every quarter shown: $244.4 million, $260.4 million, $264.2 million and then $286.3 million. The bottom line is still red. GitLab lost 22 cents a share in the July quarter, a wider loss than the 5, 2 and 3 cents of the three quarters before it.

The market is paying for the growth. GitLab carries a market value near $9.47 billion and a forward P/E of 54.7; there is no trailing P/E because the company is not profitable on a trailing basis. The next report is due Dec. 1.

The chart has turned. GitLab broke out Oct. 12 from a five-week cup, 20.4% deep, with its rim on Sept. 2 and its low on Sept. 28. The buy point is 55.65 and the range runs to 58.43. The breakout session traded 0.87 times its 50-day average. Eleven sessions later the stock closed Tuesday at 56.82, up 0.17, or 0.3%, on volume 0.39 times average, 2.1% above the buy point.

The stock is 1.8% below its 52-week high of 57.89, and its 52-week low is 18.73. It trades 15.4% above its 50-day line at 49.24 and 68.4% above its 200-day, and it finished 0.94 ATRs from the 21-day line at 53.37, an orderly trend. The RS rank is 95 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is 1.2% below its high. Shares are up 51.4% this year and 67.0% over three months.

A fund letter credited the company with easing AI disruption fears after what it called exceptional Q2 results, according to a Tuesday headline. Earlier in October, GitLab announced the foundation for what it calls the governed software factory.
The setup is in range and the trend is intact. A close under 55.65 would stall the breakout.
article.watch: The 57.89 yearly high above and the 55.65 buy point below, with earnings Dec. 1.

article.deck: Tesla closed just past the 406.28 top of its buy range, one session after moving through its 386.93 buy point.

The September quarter was soft: earnings fell 43.6% to 22 cents a share and revenue slipped 0.2% to $28.05 billion. The three quarters before earned 32, 13 and 24 cents. The forward P/E is 189.0 on a market value near $1.61 trillion.
Musk touted a Cybercab fleet expansion, according to a Tuesday headline, and another said SpaceX and Tesla are exploring a potential merger.

article.headline: Palo Alto Networks Gains 2.9% As Partners Expand Cortex And MSSP Ties
article.deck: Palo Alto sits 0.7% above its 398.98 buy point, back in a buy range that runs to 418.93.
body: Palo Alto Networks rose 11.24, or 2.9%, to 401.70, with volume 0.79 times its 50-day average. The stock broke out Oct. 2 from a seven-week cup, 19.4% deep, with its rim on Aug. 13 and its low on Sept. 2. The buy point is 398.98 and the range runs to 418.93; the close is 0.7% above the buy point. The breakout session traded 0.79 times the average.

After the breakout the stock reached a 52-week high of 432.33 and pulled back; it now sits 7.1% below that high, 17 sessions after the breakout. It trades 8.3% above its 50-day line at 370.99 and finished 0.59 ATRs from the 21-day line at 377.31. The RS rank is 94 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is 3.1% below its high. Shares are up 118.1% this year and 85.0% over 12 months.

Revenue has climbed every quarter shown, from $2.47 billion to $2.59 billion to $3.00 billion to $3.41 billion, the last up 34.4%. Earnings went the other way: a loss of 35 cents a share in the July quarter after a 22-cent loss in April, against profits of 47 and 61 cents in the two quarters before. The forward P/E is 82.3 on a market value near $328.6 billion. The next report is due Nov. 19.
NWN strengthened its Palo Alto partnership with three advanced MSSP specializations, and Horizon3 announced a NodeZero integration with Cortex XSOAR, according to Tuesday headlines.
A close back under 398.98 would stall the breakout again.
article.watch: Whether the stock holds 398.98 and can retake the 432.33 high.

stories.angle: still in buy range after breakout

article.headline: ConocoPhillips Falls 2.3% As It Plans Canadian Workforce Cuts
article.deck: ConocoPhillips is near the top of its buy range, 4.4% above the 141.72 buy point with the range ending at 148.81.
body: ConocoPhillips fell 3.41, or 2.3%, to 147.96, with volume 0.8 times its 50-day average. The stock broke out Oct. 14 from a four-week flat base, 12.8% deep, with its rim on Sept. 15 and its low on Sept. 29. The buy point is 141.72 and the range runs to 148.81; the close is 4.4% above the buy point, near the top of the range. The breakout session traded 0.85 times the average.

The 52-week high of 152.77 is 3.1% away. The stock trades 9.6% above its 50-day line at 134.97 and above the 21-day line at 141.06, finishing 1.78 ATRs from the 21-day line. The RS rank is 91 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is 8.8% below its high. Shares are up 58.1% this year and 68.1% over 12 months. The breakout is nine sessions old.

June-quarter earnings rose 107.1% to 3.23 a share on revenue up 36.8% to $19.16 billion. The three quarters before earned 1.38, 1.17 and 1.78 a share. The forward P/E is 13.7 on a market value near $177.7 billion. The next report is due Nov. 5.
The company plans Canadian workforce cuts as energy consolidation builds, according to a Tuesday headline. Another noted the stock declined while the market improved.
A move past 148.81 takes it out of the buy range; a close under 141.72 would stall the breakout.
article.watch: The 148.81 top of the range and the Nov. 5 report.

market_note: The S&P 500 rose 0.6% to 7722.6 and sits 0.3% above its 50-day line, the Nasdaq gained 1.2% to 26477.81 but closed 0.4% below its 50-day, and the Dow finished flat at 52377.57, 0.2% above the line. The S&P 500 carries 5 distribution days over the last 25 sessions and the Nasdaq and Dow 3 each, and the desk holds the market at Uptrend under pressure. Leadership is narrow but real: Amgen, ServiceNow, Apple and Berkshire Hathaway moved past buy points this week, energy owns the buy-range list with ConocoPhillips, EOG, Chevron and Exxon, and software has 84% of its names above the 50-day line while AI chips have only 38%. After hours, Robinhood fell 7.9% to 87.10, Halliburton 7.5% to 32.94, NXP Semiconductors 7.3% to 235.00 and Seagate 5.8% to 629.00, with Robinhood, NXP and Seagate all on the desk's earnings calendar for today.

chief.verdict: The leaders are tilting defensive and toward commodities: energy (avg RS 68, 86% above the 50-day) and big-cap health care are the bases working, while AI chips run an avg RS of 76 with only 38% of the group above its 50-day line. Most of today's breakouts came on soft volume (PANW 0.79, NOW 0.95, XOM 1.0) and a heavy cluster of them report inside the next week, so the risk leans to the downside on earnings gaps rather than to missed upside. The cleanest setups are the software names with earnings a month out, not the ones the score likes best.
chief.market: Uptrend under pressure with 5 S&P distribution days and the Nasdaq still 0.4% below its 50-day even after a 1.2% gain, so run half exposure at most and add only on setups with no earnings in the next five sessions.

picks.why: A 7-week cup, 19.4% deep, with RS rank 94 and the RS line only 3.1% off its high, sitting 0.7% above the 398.98 buy point and well inside the 418.93 limit. Earnings are not until 2026-11-19, so there is no report risk inside the buy range. The risk is the 0.79 breakout volume and EPS down 197.2% year over year: institutions have not shown up in size yet.
picks.entry: Buy between 398.98 and 418.93, best on a day that clears 401.70 on volume above the 6,031,876 50-day average; a close back under 398.98 on heavy volume ends the trade.

picks.why: RS rank 95 with the RS line 1.2% from its high, a 5-week cup 20.4% deep, and 2.1% above the 55.65 buy point with earnings out on 2026-12-01. Today's volume dried up to 0.39 of average just under the 57.89 52-week high, which is quiet, not distribution. The risk is that it sits 15.4% above its 50-day and still posts losses (EPS -0.22), so a market wobble hits it hard.
picks.entry: Buy on a close above 57.89 (the 52-week high) on volume above the 4,699,640 average, no higher than the 58.43 buy limit; under 55.65 the breakout has failed.

picks.why: The best-built breakout on the page: an 8-week cup, 16.2% deep, cleared on 1.11x volume, RS line 0.6% off its high, 0.2% above 447.13 with EPS up 64.9%. But earnings land 2026-11-03, the fifth session from here, and today's follow-through came on just 0.62 of average volume. The risk is buying a fresh breakout straight into the report.
picks.entry: Wait for the 2026-11-03 report; if it holds above 447.13 afterward and stays under the 469.49 limit, buy on the first up day on above-average volume.

picks.why: The aggressive entries are real: today's low touched the 50-day line and closed above it, and the handle high from 2026-10-22 sits at 825.62, 1.2% above the 816.10 close, with the standard buy point at 859.44. But earnings are 2026-10-30, three days away, and EPS was down 4.5% last quarter. Starting a position on the early entry three days before a report is a coin flip, not a setup.
picks.entry: No early entry before 2026-10-30; after the report, a clear of the 825.62 handle high with the 791.66 50-day line holding is the start, and 859.44 is the full buy point.

avoid.why: Reports 2026-10-28, tomorrow, after a breakout on 0.95x volume, 11.4% above its 50-day, and with the RS line 27.2% below its high; that is a bet on the report, not on the base.
Already at 407.46, past the 406.28 buy limit one day after breakout and 8.4% above its 21-day line, with Q3 EPS down 43.6%. The entry was 386.93, and it is gone.
A 36.6% deep cup whose 2026-10-01 breakout on 0.79x volume failed and now sits 5.5% under the 64.35 pivot; the RS rank of 97 cannot fix a base that loose.
Reports 2026-10-30 after a breakout on average volume (1.0x), fell 2.5% today, and the RS line is 13.8% off its high, which is lagging a stock at a new price high.

chief.watch: Whether the Nasdaq can close back above its 50-day line, now 0.4% below it, without the S&P adding a sixth distribution day to the five since 2026-09-28.
